title: Mapping, Filtering, and Reduction
definition: Mapping transforms each visited element, filtering retains elements that satisfy a predicate, and reduction combines a traversal into an accumulated result governed by an initial value and update rule.
purpose: Express collection intent as transformation, selection, or aggregation and verify empty and boundary behavior.
history: These operations are language-independent collection patterns implemented by loops, comprehensions, iterators, and higher-order functions.
mental_model: Map changes every card, filter chooses cards, and reduce folds the chosen cards into one summary state.
analogy: An assembly line transforms, quality control selects, and packing combines; unlike software, callbacks and sparse positions have exact language-specific rules.
common_mistakes: Using map only for side effects
industry_notes: Choose the clearest traversal; multiple declarative passes may be preferable until measurement proves a single pass necessary.
ai_notes: Require equivalence tests between loop and operation-based implementations.
interview_notes: Ask candidates to explain map/filter/reduce without library syntax.
